thread.title: 50 Worst Performing S&P 500 Constituents In November - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)

author: Ploutos
title: 50 Worst Performing S&P 500 Constituents In November - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY)
text:
As late as November 23rd, the S&P 500 ( SPY ) had produced a -2.7% return in November. On the heels of October's -6.8% return, the index had erased its year-to-date gain. A late month bounce on dovish Fedspeak and hopes for a trade war truce pushed index returns positive at +2.0% for the month. Despite this modest reversal, some index constituents still felt pressure over the course of the month. The table below lists the 50 worst performing S&P 500 constituents in November.
In October, I published the best and worst performing decile for the S&P large, mid, and small cap indices. In large cap space, the laggards list was read more than 4x as frequently as the leaders list . I say give the readers what they want, so I am producing this large cap laggards list again for November. It was a dire month for the worst performing decile in October as those stocks shed 22% on average. While November featured a modest gain for the broad index, the worst performing decile still fell 14% on average.
The laggards were led by Pacific Gas & Electric ( PCG ), which saw roughly half its value erased as the company is investigated for its role in the devastating and tragic Camp Fire. General Electric ( GE ) continued one if the worst years in its long and storied history, finishing as the third worst performer on the month.
Apple ( AAPL ), was the 10th worst performer on the month, weighing on the broad market gauge and helping the equal-weighted index ( RSP ) to outperform the capitalization weighted index on the month. Apple is now in a battle with both Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) from the crown as world's most valuable company.
It was a wide cross section of industries that represented the worst performing companies. In past months, utilities have not been represented on this laggards list, but the two California fire names - the aforementioned Pacific Gas and Edison International ( EIX ) changed that trend. Information technology and energy were heavily represented on the laggards list. Financials were under-represented, but an idiosyncratic issue in Malaysia soured the month for Goldman Sachs ( GS ).
If this information is useful to Seeking Alpha readers looking to assess bargains in the market after recent sell-offs, this spreadsheet is in a replicable format in a workbook with ready data feeds. This info is also available for other indices like the small and mid-cap stock lists published previously. I can tailor the fields and periodicity of these lists to reader needs as desired.
